q: It is claimed that the 2023 reservation amendment has already altered the composition of the lower House. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim fails: the amendment operates only after a census and the delimitation that follows
The claim succeeds: the amendment operated from the date it received assent
The claim fails: the amendment applies to the upper House and not the lower
The claim succeeds: the composition changed at the last general election
expl: The amendment is enacted but not yet operative.
why: The third option is wrong in the opposite direction, the amendment covering directly elected Houses only.
trapnote: Enacted is not operative. The census and delimitation conditions must be satisfied first.

q: Consider the ceiling on the strength of the lower House: 1-It stands at 550. 2-It was reduced from 552 in 2020. 3-The reduction followed the ending of nominated Anglo-Indian seats. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three are accurate and describe a single change.
why: The ceiling changed because two nominated seats were discontinued, which is the causal link worth retaining.
trapnote: The ceiling fell by exactly the number of nominated seats discontinued in 2020.

q: A member discloses details of custodial torture during a debate. Which statement is correct?
options: The disclosure is not protected, custody matters being outside the scope of privilege
The disclosure is protected, and the statutory safeguards stand suspended during the debate
The disclosure is protected in the House; the statutory safeguards continue to operate outside it
The disclosure is protected only where the presiding officer has granted prior permission
expl: Speech in the House is protected; the operation of statutory safeguards is unaffected.
why: The third option treats privilege as suspending the general law, which reverses the relationship entirely.
trapnote: Privilege protects what is said in the House. It neither suspends nor displaces the general law.

q: The November 2022 ruling is cited as having altered the reservation of seats in legislatures. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation succeeds: the ruling extended reservation to legislative seats
The citation fails: that ruling concerned reservation in education and employment
The citation fails: legislative seat reservation was altered in 2024 instead
The citation succeeds subject to the completion of a census
expl: Reservation of seats in legislatures rests on separate provisions and a separate amendment.
why: The fourth option imports the census condition from the 2023 amendment, a frequent cross-contamination.
trapnote: Reservation in education and employment and reservation of seats are governed separately.

q: Consider the extension of reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Tribes in legislatures: 1-It was extended in 2020. 2-The same amendment ended nominated Anglo-Indian seats. 3-The extension runs to 2030. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three limbs belong to the same amendment.
why: One amendment did two apparently unrelated things, which is why its number is asked from both directions.
trapnote: Two limbs in one amendment: extension of reservation and ending of nominated seats.

q: The 2022 reorganisation of districts in Andhra Pradesh is cited as altering the number of Assembly seats. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation succeeds: Assembly seats follow the number of districts in the State
The citation fails: Assembly strength may be altered only by a resolution of the Assembly
The citation succeeds where the Election Commission has approved the reorganisation
The citation fails: Assembly strength is altered by delimitation and not by district reorganisation
expl: District reorganisation is administrative; seat numbers follow a delimitation exercise.
why: The third option denies the citation for a wrong reason, which is a distinct kind of error.
trapnote: Administrative units and electoral constituencies are determined by different processes.

q: A claim is made that a joint sitting may be summoned to resolve disagreement over the 2023 reservation amendment. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim succeeds: a joint sitting lies for any Bill on which the Houses disagree
The claim fails: a joint sitting lies only where the upper House has rejected the Bill
The claim fails: no joint sitting lies for a Constitution Amendment Bill
The claim succeeds where the disagreement persists for more than six months
expl: Money Bills and Amendment Bills are both excluded from the joint sitting machinery.
why: The third option states a partial truth about ordinary Bills and applies it to an excluded category.
trapnote: Two categories are excluded from joint sittings. An Amendment Bill is one of them.

q: Consider the criminal statutes in force from July 2024 in relation to a sitting member: 1-They apply to a member as to any other person. 2-Privilege bars registration of an offence against a member. 3-The presiding officer must be informed of an arrest. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The statutes apply generally and the presiding officer must be informed; privilege bars nothing.
why: The second statement converts a procedural courtesy into a substantive bar, which is the common field error.
trapnote: Informing the presiding officer is a requirement of procedure. It is not a bar to process.

q: It is claimed that because the Council in Andhra Pradesh delays Bills, it may be dissolved by the Governor. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim fails: a Council cannot be dissolved and abolition requires a law of Parliament
The claim succeeds: the Governor may dissolve the Council on the advice of the Ministry
The claim fails: a Council may be dissolved only after a resolution of the Assembly
The claim succeeds where the Council has delayed a Money Bill beyond fourteen days
expl: A Council is a permanent body; it can be abolished only by a law of Parliament after a resolution.
why: The third option confuses dissolution with abolition, which are different concepts with different routes.
trapnote: A Council is never dissolved. It is abolished, and only by a law of Parliament.

q: A question asks which of these is examined by the Public Accounts Committee. Which statement is correct?
options: The estimates of expenditure submitted by ministries before the Budget
The working of public undertakings referred to it by the Speaker
The demands for grants moved by the Minister of Finance in the House
The audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General laid before the House
expl: The Committee examines the audit reports after expenditure has occurred.
why: Each wrong option names the function of a different committee or a different stage of the financial process.
trapnote: Accounts are examined after the spending. Estimates are examined before it.
